req_desc: The site presents `Vela Studio` as a one-person software studio in Marburg.
The home page reveals a philosophy statement word by word as the reader scrolls ...
The site carries no payment, no checkout, no comment, no chat, no newsletter, no search ...
An anonymous visitor reads every public route without an account ...
A `client` lists at `/account` the requests sent during a signed-in session ...
Signup creates an account with the role `client` whatever role the body claims ...
The `founder` reads every request with every attached brief ...
A denied call from a `client` session leaves the protected state unchanged ...
The seeded account `founder@example.com` holds the role `founder`.
The seeded account `client@example.com` holds the role `client`.
The seeded account `client2@example.com` holds the role `client`.
A `client` asking for the full request list is refused ...
A build request carries at most one attached brief ...
The composer at `/build-request` carries the heading `Describe the build` ...
The figure is stored in integer euro cents with the currency `eur` ...
Software, managed, eu, standard gives `1200000`.
Website, managed, eu, flexible gives `550000`.
Hosting, managed, de, standard gives `350000`.
Website, managed, de, accelerated gives `850000`.
Software plus website, handover, de, accelerated gives `2650000`.
The retired table `2026-03` sets `software` to `1000000`, `website` to `500000`, `hosting` to `250000`, keeping every other `2026-09` rule ...
The server recomputes the submitted figure from the server copy of the table ...
Each accepted request receives a reference shaped `VS-<year>-<NNNN>` ...
With scripts off, the composer posts as a plain form to `/build-request` ...
The form carries a decoy field `contact_fax` that a person never sees ...
A request starts with the status `new` ...
`GET /api/uptime/projects` answers without a session ...
The founder records a check with `POST /api/systems/{slug}/checks` ...
Missed intervals between two checks become unknown slots ...
Checks up, up, down, then up after a gap give two unknown slots with `75.00`.
Checks up, slow, degraded, up give `75.00`.
Checks up, up, down give `66.67`.
Each system stores `open_after` defaulting to `3` with `close_after` defaulting to `2` ...
Each incident entry carries `seq`, `kind`, a body, a time ...
The board lists every system as a card in feed order ...
The `/builds` page lists published build records newest delivery first ...
A diagram primitive carries `kind` of `rect`, `path` or `circle` with `role` of `accent`, `structure` or `faint` ...
The card link `Scope a build` opens the latest delivered published `software` record ...
The home argument runs in six numbered beats with the teaser below ...
The address records a reading position as `at=<section>-<percent>` ...
Under reduced motion no scroll effect loads, leaving native scrolling ...
The founder page opens with the round portrait beside the headline inside a soft amber halo ...
The legal documents set one clause per block with a fine line above each block ...
The footer list is `Home`, `About`, `Legal Notice`, `Terms`, `Status/Uptime` ...
Every internal link on every public route opens a page that exists.
Each public page view records one row carrying the route with the time ...
No response on any route sets a cookie, sign-in included ...
The founder lands on `/studio` after sign-in at `/login` ...
Interactive text reaches a contrast ratio of at least `4.5:1` against the page ground ...
The route `/builds/<slug>` shows one published build record without a session ...
A signed-out visitor opening `/account` or a `/studio` route is sent to `/login` ...
The board lists `Vela Studio` first with `Anton Ferber Portfolio` last ...
Software, handover, de, standard shows the figure `EUR 14,500` ...
A client finds a request sent during a signed-in session on `/account` with the status `new` ...
The founder downloads an attached brief from the side panel ...
The address `/builds/aurora-payroll-portal` answers not-found.
The board empty state reads `No systems available` ...
The whole site reads as one near-black sheet with darkness over decoration.
The landing blocks plus the status blocks sit on a ground one step warmer than the page ground ...
Sentences, headings, the underlined hero link, the legal back link use `Geist` ...
On load the opening block lines rise one after another from slightly below, sharpening as the lines arrive ...
The story routes are spacious with one proportional side gutter ...
Each capability card puts the drawing below the text a little below a small laptop width ...
Every interactive element shows a visible amber focus ring on keyboard focus ...
Three faint pools of warm light sit behind the page ...
Body copy is `16px`; every eyebrow is `11px` ...
The primary button is a solid amber pill with near-black text, one per page at most ...
Card `02` drawing carries a description beginning `Diagram: interface, API` ...
The next card slides over the previous card with a leading hairline under an upward shadow ...
Wheel plus keyboard scrolling glide; touch scrolling stays with the device ...
The hero meta line reads a small amber dot, `Vela Studio`, a slash, `Marburg, DE` ...
The card headings read `Software & Platforms`, `High-performing websites`, `Managed hosting, privacy-first`, `Four nodes. One jurisdiction.` ...
The founder page meta line reads `About`, a slash, `Anton Ferber` ...
The status eyebrow reads `System status` in amber ...
The seven systems in order are `Vela Studio`, `Vela Studio Finance`, `Vela Studio Analytics`, `Vela Studio Console`, `Vela Studio DB Controller`, `Vela Studio Tickets`, `Anton Ferber Portfolio` ...
The legal notice carries the eyebrow `LEGAL NOTICE` over a heading beginning `Information pursuant to` ...
The library heading reads `Builds` ...
The home title joins the studio name to `Software Made in Germany, Hosted in Europe` with a bar ...
No header menu, comparison table, questions-and-answers block, large multi-column footer, animated map or founder-notes panel is built.
The status shell carries no grain ...
The portrait stand-in is drawn in the page with an open amber arc of light ...
The front end is `Alpine.js` layered over server-rendered templates ...
Records live in `PostgreSQL` at `DATABASE_URL` ...
No second database, cache, queue, object store, identity provider or mail vendor is introduced ...
The board fetches the feed with the browser cache bypassed ...
Each font family loads one Latin subset at first paint ...
The words beside the drawing on one screen never drift apart during scrolling ...
The build request with the page-view record are the only anonymous writes ...
No downloadable asset carries a storage secret or database password ...
The `accounts` table holds an `email` unique without regard to case beside a `role`.
The `systems` table holds a unique `slug`, `name`, a unique `position`, `interval_seconds`, `open_after`, `close_after` ...
The `checks` table holds `checked_at`, `status`, `response_ms` for the owning system ...
The `incidents` table holds a unique `ref`, `opened_at`, a `resolved_at` that stays null until the incident resolves.
The `incident_entries` table holds `seq`, `kind`, `body`, `recorded_at` ...
The `build_records` table holds `slug`, `title`, `capability`, `stack`, `delivered_on`, `client_visible`, `diagram`, `published`, `published_at` ...
A measurement `metric` is `lcp_ms`, `cls`, `p95_api_ms` or `uptime_percent` ...
The `build_requests` table holds `reference`, `contact_email`, `capabilities`, `rules_version`, `indicative_minor`, `currency`, `status`, `status_changed_at` ...
The `attachments` table holds a unique `object_key`, `content_type`, `byte_size`, `sha256`, `original_name` ...
The `page_views` table holds only `route` with `viewed_at`.
The `portraits` table holds `object_key`, `content_type`, `uploaded_at`, the newest row shown.
The seed holds seven systems at interval `300` with `open_after` `3`, `close_after` `2` ...
A stored figure always equals the rule table result for the stored version ...
The seeded password `deku-demo-pw-2026` is written into `/app/USER_README.md` beside each account.
Every stored timestamp is UTC.
The product serves one studio with one founder, no second tenant.
The board offers no incident email subscription.
The product collects no field performance data from visitors.
The product carries one language with no locale switch.
The product offers no third-party scheduling page, no external booking link.
The public routes carry no cookie banner.
The product fetches no external font at run time.
The product stays responsive with a few thousand checks, requests, page-view rows.
No bitmap ships except the portrait the founder uploads.
The app is reachable at `APP_PUBLIC_URL` ...
The HTTP API is served on the same origin under `/api`.
The route `GET /api/health` returns `200` once the app is ready.
The app starts from the environment image with no manual steps.
Login credentials are written to `/app/USER_README.md`.
Empty `.browser_screenshots/` with `.downloads/` directories exist at the app root.
A production build is served, never a dev server.
The server keeps running after the session ends, detached from the shell.
The server binds `0.0.0.0`.
The app never downloads, installs, compiles or starts a backing service.
The app uses no edge functions, no persistent volumes, no fixed container names, no custom networks.
A list endpoint returns a top-level JSON array, the status envelope aside ...
The route `POST /api/auth/login` takes `email`, `password`, returning the account `role` with an `access_token`.
The route `GET /api/build-requests/mine` returns only the requests of the calling client, to a `client` only.
The route `GET /api/build-requests` returns every request, newest first, only to the `founder`.
The route `POST /api/build-requests/{reference}/status` takes `status`.
The route `POST /api/builds` takes `slug`, `title`, `capability`, `summary`, `body`, `stack`, `started_on`, `delivered_on`, `client_name`, `client_visible`, `diagram` ...
The route `POST /api/builds/{slug}/measurements` takes `metric`, `value`, `measured_on`, `source`.
The route `POST /api/studio/portrait` takes the file part `portrait`, returning the stored portrait with its `object_key`.
The route `POST /api/systems` takes `slug`, `name`, optional `interval_seconds`, `open_after`, `close_after`.
The route `GET /api/studio/builds` returns every record to the `founder`.
The route `POST /api/page-views` takes `route`.
The route `GET /api/page-views` returns views newest first to the `founder`.
The route `GET /api/builds` returns published records newest delivery first, an optional `capability` narrowing the list to that capability.
The route `GET /api/builds/{slug}` returns `measurements` beside `diagram`.
The incident detail returns `entries` carrying `seq`, `kind`, `body`, `recorded_at`.
The incident list rows carry `ref`, `system`, `opened_at`, `resolved_at`.

The route `POST /api/build-requests` takes a JSON body or a multipart form with an optional file part `attachment`, carrying `capabilities`, `posture`, `residency`, `timeline`, `budget_band`, `description`, `contact_name`, `contact_email`, `rules_version`, `indicative_minor`, `contact_fax` ...
The route `GET /api/build-requests/{reference}` returns the request with the `attachment`.
Bytes never live in memory, on local disk, in a base64 column, behind an open bucket, or under a stored object key pointing at nothing ...
The route `POST /api/builds/{slug}/publish` is `founder` only.
The route `POST /api/builds/{slug}/unpublish` is `founder` only.
The route `GET /api/build-requests/{reference}/attachment` answers only the `founder` or the owning `client`.
The route `POST /api/auth/signup` takes `email`, `password` ...
The route `POST /api/uptime/incidents/{ref}/notes` takes `body`, returning the appended entry.
